title: Sotto raises concerns over LGBT content in Grade 1 books
summary: Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III on Tuesday raised concerns regarding content related to lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) people supposedly being mentioned in books…

blocks.text: Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III on Tuesday raised concerns regarding content related to lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) people supposedly being mentioned in books for Grade 1 students.
This was brought up during the Senate plenary deliberations on the proposed P915.49 billion budget of the Department of Education (DepEd) and its attached agencies for fiscal year 2027.
During the session, Sotto flashed a photo of a Grade 1 textbook supposedly promoting an LGBT agenda.

“Some of us are concerned because masyado maaga ito para sa mga kabataan, sa elementary (it’s too early for those in elementary to be exposed to this). This debate has been going on for quite a while. We have people, I understand, advocating for both sides; you know, it's understandable. We have many friends on that particular side,” he said.
“But DepEd has to draw a line. Hindi ba masyadong mababaw ang pang-unawa ng mga elementarya para ituro kaagad ito nang ganito,” he added.
(But the DepEd has to draw a line. Isn’t the level of understanding of elementary students too limited for this to be taught to them so soon?)
Sotto said that he has nothing against the ideologies of the LGBT, but he is simply asking if lessons on LGBT should really be taught in schools.
He called on the DepEd to instead focus on subjects teaching kids respect and kindness to others, and how to prevent them from using illegal drugs.
He also suggested that the agency come up with books concentrating on anti-bullying, financial literacy, mental wellness, as well as improving learners’ reading capabilities.
“You know, siguro dapat doon ang concentrate talaga ng DepEd (DepEd should concentrate on these)--to build student resilience, emotional awareness, and mindful exercises,” Sotto said.

“Palagay ko ‘yun ang mas magandang pag-aksyahan natin ng mga libro kesa sa ganito na controversial ano because merong mga Catholic groups, Christian groups, even Muslim groups that are not in favor of having this in the elementary,” he continued.

(I think that’s a better way to use books instead of touching on controversial topics because there are Catholic groups, Christian groups, even Muslim groups that are not in favor of having this in the elementary.)

Budget sponsor Senator Bam Aquino, in response, said that topics on mental health awareness, GMRC, financial literacy, and anti-drug abuse are already being tackled in the schools at different grade levels.
“I'm sure the Secretary, upon your interpellation today, will check again the proper grade levels for these topics, Mr. President,” Aquino said.
Education Secretary Sonny Angara is in the session hall during the deliberations on DepEd’s proposed 2027 budget. —LDF, GMA News
